newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-WHEATON, MAKING COMEBACK, WINS AT WASHINGTON TOURNEY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WHEATON, MAKING COMEBACK, WINS AT WASHINGTON TOURNEY.

text.p: David Wheaton, walking the comeback trail one step at a time, rallied from behind to defeat Roberto Jabali of Brazil 2-6 6-3 6-3 in the opening round of the $675,000 Legg Mason Tennis Classic Monday.

None of the top seeds saw action as the tournament awaited the return to tennis of third seed Andre Agassi, who has played just 12 matches in 1997 and has not participated in any of this year's Grand Slam tournaments.
Defending champion Michael Chang is the top seed and Czech Petr Korda is seeded second.
Wheaton, sidelined with injuries for eight months, took having to fight his way into the main draw of a tournament in stride, winning two matches over the weekend to qualify.
"One thing I've learned after my injuries is to not expect to get it all back in a week," Wheaton said after his victory.

"When I was recuperating from surgery, it certainly crossed my mind that my career might be over," the 28-year-old Minnesota native said. "But then I thought, if at all possible, they are going to have to put me out of this game for me to leave."

In his first match back, Wheaton made it to the quarter-finals of the grass court tourney in Newport last week. His second-round opponent here is 12th-seeded Marzio Martelli of Italy, a 7-6 7-5 victor over Ivan Ljubicic of Croatia.

Wheaton, who made his first ATP Tour semifinal at the age of 20 when he beat Agassi and Jim Courier back-to-back at Stratton Mountain, Vermont, jumped from 441st in the world rankings to 66th that year, 1989. Two years later he made the semifinals at Wimbledon, earned $2.5 million and was just a couple of spots removed from the top ten.

The next few years he had hip problems and he leveled off just inside the top 50. Last year, his left Achilles' tendon gave out, a bone spur developed in the heel and he needed surgery. His ranking dropped to 232 on the computer and he had to compete in qualifying tournaments.
Another player recovering from injury, Patrick McEnroe, fell to Davide Scala of Italy 6-1 4-6 7-5 in his first tournament since shoulder surgery in February.
Fourteenth-seeded American Vince Spadea beat France's Stephane Siminan 2-6 6-1 6-1 and 15th-seeded South African Neville Godwin got past Argentina's Gaston Etlis 4-6 6-4 6-4.

Veteran Bryan Shelton had a scare in the featured night match before subduing recent high school graduate Alex Kim 7-6 6-3. Kim won a Wildcard Challenge tournament event over 170 others to make it into the 56-man field and is slated to enroll at three-time national collegiate men's tennis champion Stanford in September.
